title: KV key shaping heuristics and safe-config apply/rollback automation
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Objective: Build a repeatable system that recommends KV/prefix cache key shapes and TTL policies using hit-rate modeling and offline replay, and that can safely apply and rollback cache configuration changes in production. Scope includes: (1) offline hit-rate simulator and estimator for alternative keying strategies, (2) TTL policy optimizer that recommends tiered TTL buckets, and (3) an automated safe-apply workflow with canary rollout, real-time telemetry gates, and automatic rollback hooks. This ticket focuses on the engineering design, a reference implementation for a single critical route (chat.complete), and integration with the console rollout APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can ingest 7 days of request traces and output estimated hit-rate delta for at least 3 candidate keying strategies
Automated TTL optimizer produces per-route recommendations (hot/warm/cold TTL buckets) and expected token-savings estimate
Safe-apply pipeline can deploy cache config to 1% -> 10% -> 100% traffic with automated rollback on predefined metric breaches
End-to-end smoke test in staging reproduces expected hit-rate improvement for the chat.complete route by >= 8% without latency regressions
Documentation and a Console UI panel show recommended key shapes, expected savings, and a one-click apply with rollback controls
design_decisions: Use offline trace replay with probabilistic batching to estimate prefix-level cache hit rates rather than full live A/B for initial tuning
Represent key shapes as ordered attribute vectors (model_id, prompt_signature_hash, user_bucket, tenant_tier) to allow compact hashing and prefix grouping
Tiered TTLs per prefix: default hot TTL=60s, warm TTL=300s, cold TTL=3600s; optimizer may suggest shifts based on request churn
Safe-apply will integrate with existing rollout service to use canary traffic routing plus a sidecar metric-checker that can mark a rollout as failed
Store applied config artifact in immutable config registry with version tags and rollback csn (change sequence number)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Run offline simulator for 7-day traces and publish recommendations to /console/recommendations
Stage 1: Apply TTL/key changes to staging and validate with synthetic and sampled production-like traces
Stage 2: Canary 1% traffic for 30 minutes with gates: cache hit-rate delta >= 5% or token cost reduction >= 3% AND no p50 latency increase > 5%
Stage 3: Ramp to 10% for 1 hour; if metrics hold, ramp to 100% in controlled steps
Rollback: immediate revert to prior config on gate failure and run automated diagnostic job to capture traces for postmortem
telemetry_and_metrics: Primary: KV prefix hit-rate (per-minute), token-per-request cost, cache eviction rate
Reliability: p50/p95 latency for affected routes, request error rate
Safety gates: relative change vs baseline for hit-rate, latency, and 5xxs. Thresholds encoded in rollout policy
Observability: sample-level traces linked to applied config version and canary id for root cause analysis
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive key coarsening increases collision and reduces personalization -> Mitigation: simulator flags personalization-sensitive keys and excludes from grouping

Risk: TTL misconfiguration causes stale or semantically incorrect cached outputs -> Mitigation: require route-level schema checks and human sign-off for routes that emit non-idempotent structured outputs
Risk: Rollout gating reacts to noisy signals -> Mitigation: use rolling windows and smoothed metrics plus minimum sample sizes before decisions
Risk: Storage pressure from expanded prefix index -> Mitigation: estimate additional memory from simulator and set conservative initial limits with autoscale alerts
